chapters.title: Hub
chapters.description: Links every chapter with a one-line description and a locally-persisted progress checklist.

chapters.title: How the HLD Interview Actually Works
chapters.description: What's actually being scored; a repeatable framework (requirements → capacity estimate → API → high-level design → deep dive → trade-offs); functional vs non-functional requirements; back-of-envelope capacity math with 2+ worked examples; common failure modes; what reads as EM-level vs IC-level.

chapters.title: Scale From Zero to Millions of Users
chapters.description: The 10-revision build-up from a single server to a sharded, multi-region, event-driven system. Light-theme rebuild of the reference chapter.

chapters.title: Networking & Communication Building Blocks
chapters.description: DNS; HTTP/HTTPS; REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC vs WebSockets vs SSE vs long-polling with a decision table; L4 vs L7 load balancers; reverse proxy vs API gateway; CDN.

chapters.part: Part II — Core Scalability Building Blocks
chapters.title: Caching Deep Dive
chapters.description: Cache-aside, read-through, write-through, write-back, write-around; eviction (LRU/LFU/FIFO); thundering herd and mitigations; Redis vs Memcached; real examples.

chapters.part: Part II — Core Scalability Building Blocks
chapters.title: Load Balancing, Rate Limiting & Consistent Hashing
chapters.description: LB algorithms; rate limiting algorithms (token/leaky bucket, fixed/sliding window) with a real API example; consistent hashing with virtual nodes.

chapters.part: Part II — Core Scalability Building Blocks
chapters.title: Partitioning, Sharding & Replication
chapters.description: Range/hash/directory sharding; replication topologies. MySQL (Vitess) and MongoDB shown side by side with a comparison table.

chapters.title: Relational Databases Deep Dive (MySQL)
chapters.description: Indexing (B-tree vs hash); ACID; isolation levels and the anomalies each prevents; MVCC; locking; normalization vs denormalization; replication and failover.

chapters.title: Document & Key-Value NoSQL Deep Dive
chapters.description: MongoDB schema design (embed vs reference), aggregation pipeline, indexing; Redis data structures beyond caching; DynamoDB partition keys, quorum reads/writes, GSIs.

chapters.title: Wide-Column & Graph NoSQL
chapters.description: Cassandra ring architecture, gossip, LSM-tree + compaction, tunable consistency (R+W>N); brief HBase; Neo4j graph modeling with a concrete query example.

chapters.title: Data Lakes, Data Warehouses & Lakehouses
chapters.description: OLTP vs OLAP; lake vs warehouse vs lakehouse; file formats (Parquet/ORC/Avro) and table formats (Delta/Iceberg/Hudi); ETL vs ELT; one full worked pipeline end to end.

chapters.title: Search, Time-Series & NewSQL
chapters.description: Elasticsearch inverted index vs a DB index; time-series DBs; NewSQL (Spanner/CockroachDB/Vitess/TiDB); closes with a polyglot-persistence example (Uber).

chapters.title: CAP Theorem, Consistency & Consensus
chapters.description: CAP with concrete per-system picks; PACELC; consistency models with real examples; Paxos and Raft explained simply but correctly.

chapters.title: Distributed Transactions & Coordination
chapters.description: 2PC/3PC; Saga (choreography vs orchestration) with a worked checkout example; idempotency; vector clocks/Lamport timestamps; distributed locks and split-brain; quorum; gossip; heartbeats.

chapters.part: Part V — Messaging, Microservices & Cross-Cutting Concerns
chapters.title: Messaging & Event-Driven Architecture
chapters.description: Queues vs pub-sub; Kafka deep dive (partitions, consumer groups, ISR, exactly-once); SQS/RabbitMQ comparison; event sourcing & CQRS; outbox pattern; backpressure.

chapters.part: Part V — Messaging, Microservices & Cross-Cutting Concerns
chapters.title: Microservices & Resiliency Patterns
chapters.description: Monolith vs microservices vs modular monolith decision framework; service discovery; API gateway; circuit breaker/retry/timeout/bulkhead; strangler fig; BFF; sidecar; service mesh.

chapters.part: Part V — Messaging, Microservices & Cross-Cutting Concerns
chapters.title: Security, Observability & Reusable Building Blocks
chapters.description: AuthN vs authZ; OAuth2/OIDC; JWT vs sessions; encryption; API security. Logs/metrics/traces and SLI/SLO/SLA. Reusable primitives: ID generation, geohashing, typeahead, distributed rate limiter and lock.

chapters.title: Problem Bank: Social & Content
chapters.description: Twitter/X, Instagram, TikTok-style feed, Reddit, YouTube/Netflix-style streaming, live comments/voting — full 11-part write-ups.

chapters.title: Problem Bank: Messaging & Real-Time
chapters.description: WhatsApp/Messenger, Slack/Discord, notification system, Google-Docs-style collaborative editing, live auction/bidding — full 11-part write-ups.

chapters.title: Problem Bank: Marketplace & Location
chapters.description: Uber/Lyft, food delivery, Maps-style ETA/routing, Yelp-style nearby search, hotel/Airbnb booking, ticket booking with seat-level concurrency — full 11-part write-ups.

chapters.title: Problem Bank: Infra Building Blocks as Interview Questions
chapters.description: URL shortener, Pastebin, rate limiter, distributed cache, web crawler, job scheduler, message queue, key-value store, unique ID generator, distributed lock service, leaderboard, ad-click aggregation, log aggregation — full 11-part write-ups.

chapters.title: Problem Bank: Payments, Search & EM-Scale Systems
chapters.description: Payment gateway, Splitwise, digital wallet, e-commerce checkout/inventory, ad exchange/RTB, search engine, recommendation system, news aggregator, plus EM-scale org problems (multi-region platform, feature flags, CI/CD, monolith→microservices migration, multi-tenant SaaS, internal dev platform, global config) — full 11-part write-ups.

chapters.title: Rapid-Fire Problem Index
chapters.description: 150+ additional named problems mapped to pattern family + one-line approach, for fast pattern-matching without full write-ups.
